failure_modes: Selecting a temporal blend or temporal region index would be a descriptive, unvalidated change that could shift regional attention without evidence of final affinity benefit.
Changing pointcloud_delta_A or teacher_neighbors without read spatial-scale or dispersion evidence could displace surrounding coordinates and increase strain without affinity gain.
Treating a large first/last rate z-value as a monotone coordinate reward direction would misread a temporal derivative as a spatial gradient.
rationale: D1.2: The only registered time-conditioned options are temporal_region_index (C008) and temporal_teacher_blend (C009-C011), which change regional attention at observed score nodes or blend the observed-teacher coordinate reward; they do not change teacher coordinates or dose. The inspected continuous trends are coordinate contrasts over the observed window with extrapolation disallowed, multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts, so no validated time-conditioned rule is established against the stationary incumbent; a temporal derivative is not a spatial gradient and cannot justify a coordinate direction. D2.1/D2.2: No spatial-scale, uncertainty, intact-teacher dispersion or joint-geometry diagnostics were read, so a distance-response curvature (C001-C003), regional emphasis (C004) or teacher-neighborhood width (C005-C007) cannot be justified; neighbor count is not a bandwidth and the fixed temperatures and teacher provenance are preserved. D4.1: The incumbent already uses teacher_neighbors=4 and pointcloud_delta_A=1.0 with the declared endpoint-VJP reward; the supplied evidence provides no defensible expected advantage over it, so retaining the incumbent is the evidence-supported choice. D4.2: A narrower or broader neighborhood or a larger delta would risk unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates without demonstrated affinity benefit, and the affinity-first priority is not served by an unsupported coordinate edit.
